From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Candidate slate and proposed offer bands for runtime infra roles

Mike / Kim —

Following up from our sync this morning. We have two strong finals for the runtime infra hiring slate: Asha Rao (senior infra SWE, strong LLM-gpu infra background) and a second caller-track candidate (internal referral) — I'll call them Candidate B for now.

Quick summary below (more details in attached Candidate_Profile_Asha_Redacted.pdf and the comp calculations workbook):

- Asha Rao — target hire for kernel/serving team. Profile: 7+ years, worked on low-latency beam search and KV cache optimizations at previous employer. Ask: $220k base, 15% bonus target, RSU-equivalent $180k over 4 years.
- Candidate B — senior-ish but fewer specialized infra heuristics; closer to band S3 mid. Ask: $180k base, 10% bonus, RSU-equivalent $90k.

Constraints & asks:
- We have two open approved slots in the runtime budget for Q3 but the comp bands are tight if we go above the normal midpoint for Asha.
- Kimberly: can we get sign-off to stretch band for Asha to the top of S4 for base + additional sign-on to bridge?
- Neha: assuming we greenlight, recruiting wants to send offers next week (5/25) to avoid losing momentum.

Requested action:
1) Kim — confirm whether payroll/comp can accommodate Asha at $220k base + $50k one-time sign-on (total first-year cash cadence) and the RSU packet we suggested in the workbook.
2) Mike — can you approve routing Asha through the VP sign-off lane (Marissa) for an exception if needed?

Attachments: Candidate_Profile_Asha_Redacted.pdf, Offer_Calculations_May2026.xlsx

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Runtime Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Mike —

Thanks for the summary and the workbook. I reviewed the numbers. High-level notes:

- Asha: base at $220k is above midpoint for S4 but still within range if we treat this as a strong market adjustment hire. The combination you propose (220 base + 50k sign-on + 180k RSU over 4y) is OK if Marissa approves a band exception. Finance flagged the sign-on as a one-time acceleration vs. recurring comp.
- Candidate B: falls neatly into S3 mid; we can extend without exception at $180k base + standard RSU banding.

Two considerations:
1) For Asha, we should split the sign-on into a $30k immediate + $20k retention tied to 12 months to reduce churn risk.
2) Please prepare a one-page justification for Marissa that includes impact/urgency and comparable market comps.

If you can get that doc to me by EOD Friday (5/21), I will route to Marissa for an expedited decision.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Total Rewards

Marissa —

Forwarding Marcus and Kim's thread. TL;DR: we have a high-signal candidate (Asha Rao) who is above our normal S4 midpoint; comp ask: $220k base + $50k sign-on (propose split) + RSU ~$180k 4y. Marcus argues critical for kernel/low-latency work (reduces p50 latency on long-tail seqs and will unblock model rollout timelines).

Why this needs exec exception:
- Recruiting: candidate has other late-stage offers and wants a decision this week.
- Impact: Asha's background maps 1:1 to our current kernel optimizations; lost hire will push roadmap ~2 quarters.
- Budget: we have a Q3 headcount slot and can absorb the comp delta within the runtime pool if exception approved.

Attached is a short justification and comp workbook (Offer_Calculations_May2026.xlsx). If you can OK an exception to top-of-band + $50k sign-on (we'll do $30k upfront + $20k retention), we can get an acceptance and close the role before next week.

Appreciate speedy read — tagging Neha to prepare offer paperwork if we get sign-off.

-Mike
